title: Nappies, wipes and baby food
text: Supermarkets and pharmacies sell them in most places. Formula brands can differ abroad, so if your baby is fussy about theirs, bring enough for the whole trip.

title: Clothes
text: A big muslin, one of your T-shirts or a cheap outfit from a local shop will do until you can wash.

title: Medicines
text: Before you go, take a photo of the labels on your family’s medicines, so a local pharmacist can see exactly what you use.

title: A cot
text: Ask where you’re staying. If there isn’t one, the Lullaby Trust has advice on making a safer sleep space away from home.

title: A passport
text: This one can’t be improvised. If a British passport is lost or stolen abroad, you may be able to get an emergency travel document.

title: Their comforter
text: The one thing worth checking twice before you leave. If you have a spare, pack it in a different bag.
